title: Imaging and quantitative analysis of integrin-dependent cell-matrix adhesions
protocol: Coat coverslips with the desired ECM protein as described in step 3 of prepare buffers, cell culture media, and substrates.
Trpsinize cells.
Seed appropriate cell density in culture medium on coated coverslips in a 24-well plate.
Place seeded plates in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Aspirate the medium and wash once with PBS containing MgCl2/CaCl2 to remove medium and/or serum components.
Fix with 500 μL of 4% PFA for 15 min at 20°C.
Wash cells 2 times with PBS.
Permeabilize with 500 μL of 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash away Triton with 2 washes in PBS.
Block non-specific binding with 0.1 M glycine in PBS for 2 h at 20°C.
Put one coverslip (with cells down) on each drop of antibody solution for staining.
Handle coverslips using tweezers with a pointed tip when placing them in the antibody solution.
Incubate coverslips for 45–60 min at 20°C.
Place coverslips back in PBS containing 0.2% gelatin in the 12-well plate with cells facing up.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS containing 0.2% gelatin for 10 minutes.
Dilute secondary antibodies in PBS containing 0.2% gelatin and pipette drops on parafilm.
Place coverslips on antibody solutions.
Incubate for 30–60 min at 20°C in the dark.
Transfer coverslips to plate as in step 15.
Wash coverslips three times with PBS containing 0.2% gelatin.
Wash coverslips twice with PBS.
Mount coverslips with cells face-down in 10% Mowiol on object slide, using approximately 10–20 μL of Mowiol for 12-mm coverslips.
Let Mowiol harden for at least 16 hours at room temperature.
Clean the non-cell-side of the mounted coverslip with a tissue moistened with ethanol.
Store coverslips at 4°C or −20°C.
Select the 63× objective.
Apply immersion oil type F on coverslip and place upside down in the microscope stage insert.
Select the appropriate laser lines.
Set laser/gain and other confocal settings.
Select the basal focal plane to focus on cell-matrix adhesions and optimize laser and gain settings.
Perform line or frame averaging to reduce noise and enhance specific signal.
Split the merged image containing FA and F-actin channels into single channel images using Image > Color > Split channels.
Perform background subtraction using Process > Subtract background.
Generate a mask on the F-actin channel with the segmented cell to analyze by drawing a line around the cell boundary with the Freehand Selection Tool.
Save the selection with Edit > Selection > Add To Manager.
Create a new image using File > New > Image (Type: 8-bit, Fill with: Black, Width/Height: same as FA image) > OK.
Select the saved cell boundary from the region of interest manager.
Ensure that the foreground color is white using the Color Picker Tool.
Fill the region in the new image using Edit > Fill.
Save using the same name as the corresponding FA image but append "_mask" to the end.
Analyze data.
Close ImageJ.
Open .csv files.
Convert pixel values to real physical values (microns).
Set a cut-off for adhesion size to exclude unrealistically small focal adhesions.
Exclude focal adhesions that are unrealistically large or improperly segmented.
Create graphs directly in Excel or using GraphPad Prism.

Transduce GE11 cells expressing wild-type integrin β1 or mutant β1Y795A with a construct encoding mCherry-vinculin, as described in lentiviral transduction for stable expression of fluorescent adhesion proteins or shRNAs.
Seed cells on large circular coverslips (24 mm diameter) that have been coated with FN (or another appropriate ECM protein) as described in prepare buffers, cell culture media, and substrates.
Replace the medium approximately 1 h before starting to set up the microscope.

Note: To increase cell motility and dynamic adhesion behavior, cells can be serum-starved prior to the experiment for 1–4 h, then re-stimulated with fresh medium containing serum shortly before onset of the experiment.
Cover the coverslip with cells into the coverslip chamber of the microscope.
Prewarm and atmospherically stabilize the microscope at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Select appropriate laser lines and settings (intensity, time interval, etc).
Choose excitation wavelength of 561 nm for mCherry, exposure time 283 ms, laser intensity 18%, interval 1 min, total imaging 45 min, angle 68°, penetration depth 90 nm.
Select xyz positions on the coverslip and save to positions list.
Ensure all positions are in focus using hardware autofocus control AFC if necessary.
Start the experiment.
Transduce HUVECs with a scrambled sequence or shRNAs to suppress expression of Arg/Abl2 as described in lentiviral transduction for stable expression of fluorescent adhesion proteins or shRNAs.
Replace medium with fresh culture medium containing 1 μg/mL puromycin 24 hours after transduction.
Collect cells and microporate them with GFP-tensin-1, as described in transient expression of fluorescent proteins in cells with stable gene suppression, 48 hours after transduction.
Seed cells in medium containing puromycin in a 6-well plate.
Coat an 8-well Lab-Tek chamber with fibronectin (FN) as described in prepare buffers, cell culture media, and substrates.
Harvest cells from a confluent well in a final volume of 1 mL culture medium with puromycin at 72 hours after transduction/24 hours after microporation.
Distribute the cells in different densities over 4 Lab-Tek chamber wells.
Add 100 μL, 200 μL, 300 μL, or 400 μL of cell suspension per well.
Fill up to 500 μL with cell culture medium by adding 400 μL, 300 μL, 200 μL, or 100 μL per well, respectively.
Look at wells under an inverted tissue culture microscope at low magnification and select those that have similar cell density for the experiment.
Replace medium with 400 μL of fresh medium without puromycin 96 h after transduction/48 h after microporation.
Allow cells to stabilize for at least 2 h before adding thrombin.
Apply immersion oil type N on the 63× objective.
Start the experiment.
Lift the lid of the Lab-Tek chamber very carefully 5 minutes after starting the experiment.
Check live whether the correct positions are still being imaged.
Add 100 μL of 2.5 U/mL thrombin to a well containing 400 μL of medium, achieving a final concentration of 0.5 U/mL thrombin.
Check live whether the correct positions are still being imaged.
Place the lid back very carefully.
Bend a fine gel-loading tip to facilitate pipetting into the Lab-Tek chamber wells while the sample is on the microscope stage.
Capture images with the same settings for all conditions, optimizing settings first on the control condition when comparing different conditions.
Use BSL-2 imaging facilities if imaging is performed shortly after transduction.
Express integrin β4 with an eGFP tag in PA-JEB keratinocytes for live-cell imaging.
Treat cells with 50 ng/mL EGF to stimulate proliferation and migration.
Image cells by TIRF microscopy using methods described for HD dynamics.
Place large circular coverslips into the wells of a 6-well plate.
Collect and seed PA-JEB cells expressing β4-eGFP on the coverslips in KGM.
Incubate the cells for at least one day in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Replace the KGM with DMEM/FCS.
Incubate the cells for an additional day in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Place the coverslips with cells in an Attofluor™ Cell Chamber (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for live-cell imaging.
Mount the chamber in a 35 mm diameter stage holder of a confocal microscope adapted for live-cell imaging.
Apply one drop of immersion oil type N on a 63× (NA 1.4) oil objective.
Prewarm and atmospherically stabilize the microscope at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Select appropriate laser lines and settings based on experimental purpose, cell type, stimulus, fluorescent protein expression levels, fluorophore intensity, and adhesion structure to be analyzed.
Use a 488 nm laser for illumination and an emission range of 500–550 nm for detection of β4-eGFP.
Record fluorescent and differential interference contrast (DIC) images every 5 minutes for 12 hours.
Select xy positions using a linearly encoded motorized stage and save to positions list.
Image several different fields per condition.
Use hardware autofocus control if necessary.
Start the experiment to image frames in the absence of EGF.
Add EGF (50 ng/mL) very carefully 30 minutes after starting the experiment.
Resume imaging for the desired time.
Capture images with the same settings for all conditions.
Optimize settings on the control condition first.
Note: BSL-2 imaging facilities are required if imaging is performed shortly after transduction.
Note: Normal behavior of adhesion complexes and proper capture of their dynamics are influenced by many different factors.
Note: Risks of live-cell fluorescent imaging include signal bleaching and phototoxicity, which can be minimized with a number of approaches.
Seed A431 cells on large circular coverslips (24 mm diameter) in DMEM/FCS.
Refresh the medium approximately 1 hour before starting to set up the microscope.
Secure coverslip in an Attofluor™ Cell Chamber (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Apply one drop of immersion oil type N on the 63× Plan Apochromat (NA 1.4) oil objective.

Select the appropriate laser lines (for instance for excitation at 488 nm) and settings (intensity, time interval, etc), depending on expression levels and dynamics of the protein investigated, as well as cell type and stimuli.
Record 2 images of selected ROIs as pre-bleaching controls.
Switch to high-laser power for bleaching the selected ROI.
Record a post-bleaching time-lapse series every 15 seconds during 5 minutes to monitor fluorescence recovery.
Subtract background fluorescence from measured intensities for analysis.
Normalize curves to the mean value before bleaching.
Culture cells in appropriate medium as described.
Seed cells on coated circular coverslips (12 mm diameter) in a 24 well plate.
Perform analysis of multiple ROI’s per cell and perform analysis of multiple cells per condition.
Follow integrin behavior using live-cell labeling with antibodies.
Assess integrin endocytosis and recycling by pulse-chase assays.
Plate cells in culture medium and place at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Wash cells with ice-cold serum-free medium in the cold room.
Incubate cells with primary antibody TS2/16 conjugated to CY5 for labeling β1 integrins, diluted in ice-cold serum-free medium.
Incubate cells with primary antibody 439-9B conjugated to FITC for labeling β4 integrins, diluted in ice-cold serum-free medium.
Labeling should occur for 1 hour on ice and in the cold room.
Transfer 1 or 2 coverslips directly after labeling to a well containing 4% PFA.
Place coverslips in serum-free medium at 37°C to allow internalization of labeled cell-surface integrins.
Take out coverslips after appropriate time-points and transfer them to 4% PFA for fixation.
Fix coverslips as required for further processing.
Process coverslips further if desired (for instance, to label nuclei, adhesion complex components, or intracellular compartments).
Mount coverslips on microscope slides as described in staining of cell-matrix adhesions for immunofluorescence imaging.
Image the coverslips by confocal microscopy as described in confocal imaging of cell-matrix adhesions in fixed cells.
